# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 66 (Bu-Vb Pc66)
**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc66
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 66
**Title (English, from literature):** Traveling with thieves

**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The rule is shared across early Buddhist monastic codes. Direct parallels exist in the Bhikkhu Pātimokkhas and Vibhaṅgas of the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, Lokottaravāda, and Dharmaguptaka traditions across Sanskrit, Chinese, Tibetan, and Gāndhārī, as well as in the corresponding Bhikkhunī rules (such as Pali Bhikkhunī Pācittiya 145) [SuttaCentral; Hüsken 1997]. Internally, DharmaNexus records hundreds of matching segments within the Pali canon, sharing its longest textual overlaps with Pācittiya 27, Pācittiya 67 (§1.12–2.1.4), Pācittiya 64, and Pācittiya 28 [DharmaNexus]. Cross-linguistic matches in DharmaNexus confirm correspondences with Tibetan Vinaya texts, including the Tibetan *Vinayavibhaṅga* (D3-3), the *Pratimokṣasūtrapaddhati* (D4104), and Guṇaprabha's *Vinayasūtra* (D4117) [DharmaNexus]. The rule has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
